newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU defers decision on China rights criticism.
newsitem.headline: EU defers decision on China rights criticism.

text.p: The European Union on Monday put off sponsoring its annual United Nations resolution condemning China for human rights abuses despite signs of unusually robust support from the United States.

EU officials said a decision to sponsor the resolution -- which it has done for the past six years at the U.N. Commission on Human Rights -- would now be put off until a later meeting, probably next month.
The resolution, though symbolic, is considered highly offensive by China.

France delayed the decision at an EU foreign ministers meeting when French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette argued that more time was needed for concerted action to be agreed with other countries, notably the United States.
Paris indicated that after six years of sponsorship it may be time for the main sponsor of the resolution to come from outside the 15-nation EU.

One diplomat said de Charette had also suggested during a long discussion with his colleagues that they tended to be too hard on China compared with their more measured approaches to countries such as Iran and Syria.
The delay came as Washington indicated that it would be willing this year to throw its full force behind the resolution.

British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind told reporters that the United States had said it would take such as stance. Diplomats said U.S. officials visiting Beijing with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright had told representatives of the Dutch EU presidency that there had been no signs of improvement in China's stance during talks there.
The Americans had said they would sponsor the resolution, a decision that was transmitted by the Dutch to the EU ministers in Brussels.
Diplomats said that despite the delay there was widespread concern over China's human rights record among the EU countries and that it was likely a resolution would be agreed later.
The ministers nonetheless issued an uncritical statement saying that the EU regretted the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping and praised his contributions to his country's development.

"He stimulated economic development, raised the standard of living and prosperity of the Chinese population and played a large role in the opening up of China to the international community," the statement said.
